newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka stocks surge, rally seen continuing for now.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka stocks surge, rally seen continuing for now.

text.p: Dhaka stocks have soared to record highs, driven by a wave of fresh funds flowing into the market, and analysts say the bull run may continue for the time being.
The benchmark Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) share price index closed 31.96 points or 2.64 percent higher at 1,249.9 on Sunday, an all-time high, on turnover of 167.2 billion taka.
The market capitalisation also crossed the $2.0 billion mark on Sunday, compared with only $452 million at the end of 1994.

The rise has been fuelled by liberalisation of investment rules by the newly elected centrist government, which has encouraged small investors to pour funds into the market and driven up stock prices, brokers said.
Shares also opened higher on Monday, brokers said, as investors bought up engineering stocks. The market trades on Sunday as Friday is the weekend in Moslem Bangladesh.
A month ago, the DSE index was trading around the 1,145 level.
"The share index has continued to surge forward on the back of frenzied local retail buying," said Brenda Trenowden, head of research at Peregrine Capital Bangladesh Limited, on Monday.

Trenowden said there had been considerable oversubscription in recent primary issues, reflecting strong interest in stocks, and predicted demand would stay keen, although the market may be due for a correction down the road.

"Given this momentum, we believe that there are still new funds waiting to come into the market, which should ensure a continuation of the current bull run for at least another month," she told Reuters.
But Trenowden said foreign institutional investors remained sceptical about the country's often volatile politics and the valuation of share prices.
"Foreign institutional sentiment, however, remains negative based on perceived political risk and the unjustifiably high valuations in the market," she said.
She said the Dhaka Stock Exchange was fully valued on a fundamental basis and could be due for a correction.
Dvai Ghose, a senior strategist with Peregrine, said a sustained surge in cement and engineering stocks had helped to push the market up to record highs.
He singled out the pharmaceuticals, textiles and tobacco sectors as attractive investments.
Khurshid Alam, a former DSE chairman, said there had been a huge flow of idle money into the market as new investors looking for good returns on their money piled into the market.
"The current market surge is not necessarily related to the economic fundamentals of the companies. There is a combination of so many factors," he said.
Alam, himself a DSE broker, said retail investors were chasing available shares, in the absence of new issues.
Brokers said the market had started rising since the new government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina took power on June 23 following an internationally supervised free-and-fair election.
The government recently lifted a restriction on the trade of initial public offerings (IPOs) by foreign investors, and waived gains tax on the sale of bonus shares.

The government also came up with an investment-friendly budget last month, reducing import tariffs on industrial machinery and raw materials. A climate of political stability in the wake of the elections has also contributed to the positive mood on the stock market.
